summary: The approach is general and appropriately safety-focused, but the compatibility gate can exclude candidates using a product-type comparison that is not an explicit usable constraint, violating its own fail-open contract.
issues: `evaluate_candidate_compatibility()` always compares `product_type`, even when it is `other`. Yet `usable_constraint_fields()` deliberately treats `other` as unusable. Thus an in-scope extraction with `product_type='other'` plus DN/connection can reject all recognized catalog products solely on the non-constraint type value.

The type fallback treats any nonempty unclassifiable name as positive type evidence, making it `contradictory` rather than `unverifiable`. This conflicts with the stated requirement that incomplete/unparseable catalog metadata must remain eligible and plausibly contributes to the 28% public wrong-NOT_FOUND rate.

Diagnostic `candidate_id` values are original retrieval positions, while reranker candidate IDs are renumbered after filtering. This makes audit records misleading unless explicitly modeled as retrieval rank.
fix_plan: Only evaluate product type when `constraints.product_type != 'other'`; otherwise omit its check entirely.

Classify an unrecognized candidate type as unverifiable unless there is explicit, reliable evidence for a different canonical type; add focused tests with nonempty but unclassifiable names/properties.
Either rename diagnostic `candidate_id` to `retrieval_rank` or record both original retrieval rank and post-gate reranker ID; test a case where an earlier candidate is excluded.
Re-run the public harness and inspect gate diagnostics by excluded field before considering promotion.
next_direction: Constraint gating remains a credible direction, but prioritize fail-open handling for incomplete or uncanonical catalog metadata and use per-field exclusion/abstention counts to identify which constraint is driving wrong-NOT_FOUND outcomes.
